L9: # Register your interest in our dog cancer trial
L10: 
L11: We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

L16: ## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.

L20: Rosie

L22: The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.

L24: It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.

L3: # Perth dogs helping to fight cancer
L4: 
L5: Associate Professor Lesterhuis said the gel, developed with the help of chemists at The University of Western Australia, could revolutionise the way solid tumours were treated.
L6: 
L7: 【5†Image: a dog being treated in a medical facility】
L8: 
L9: Immunotherapy is the new holy grail of cancer treatment – using the patient’s own immune system to fight the disease.
L10: But this revolutionary therapy has had little impact on solid tumours like sarcoma, the third most common cancer in children. Now, a world-first trial at The Kids Research Institute Australia could change that – all with the help of man’s best friend.
L11: 
L12: The busy pre-surgery area of Perth Veterinary Specialists in Osborne Park is perhaps the last place you’d expect to be ground zero for a clinical trial that could save the lives of thousands of kids around the world.

L7: 
L8: ##
L9: ## Why refer your patients?
L10: 
L11:   * The therapy (GCN2-IN-6) has been carefully tested in preclinical studies and is well-tolerated.
L12:   * Your referred patients will receive standard surgical care plus the investigational therapy.
L13:   * Participation contributes valuable data for advancing cancer treatments in both cats and humans.
